results.why: The 07:29:58 opens-on-vehicle cell flown by a pilot holding 2 m/s EAST (review of 69c27bd, P2). The way out is then east, and the corridor-survey-route edge at x = 80 is only 9 m past the school zone's ring at x = 71: in the plain library geometry another hard rule lies within the cap's straight 5 s forecast (20 m) of the exit. On 69c27bd the floored escape was re-checked on that straight forecast, the cap was refused, the escape slowed (3.75, 3.5 ... 2.25 m/s, the speed whose straight forecast ends at x = 80), and from x = 70 the pilot's own 2 m/s broke the corridor and the FSM went Normal > Brake > Loiter: 16 ticks inside the polygon and 4.0 s to safe on the grant arm (8 / 2.9 s on the 3 s arm), with P0 escape 0, against 5 / 2.8 s (7 on the 3 s arm) on 7c9c9e6, every tick escalated and the hold transit at the cap. The escape from a window that opened on the aircraft is now judged as it is flown: out of the ring, then a stop (one forecast step, then 3 m/s^2; guardrail/shield.py Shield._shaped_escape), which ends at x = 74.1 on the grant arm (75.7 on the 3 s arm), short of the corridor edge, so the cap flies. Measured 2026-10-22: 5 / 2.8 s on the grant arm and 7 / 2.8 s on the 3 s arm - 7c9c9e6's counts exactly - 0 P0 escapes, no refused cap or floor, the FSM Normal until the aircraft is out of the ring; then the pilot's 2 m/s east, whose own forecast breaks the corridor from 10 m short of its edge, is projected and the FSM brakes (Normal > Brake, G1), which is the corridor rule doing its job outside the zone, not the escape. Bounds: ticks inside at most 7 (the 3 s arm's count; a family gate is one bound for both arms, and tests/test_window_opens_on.py pins each arm at 7c9c9e6 + 1 for 1 and 2 m/s east and 1 m/s west), time to safe at most 2.9 s, never censored, and no tick refusing the cap or the floor.
